newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes weaker on swaps, banks cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes weaker on swaps, banks cover.

text.p: Mexico's 24- and 48-hour peso contracts closed slightly weaker Wednesday due to swaps and banks covering short dollar positions, traders said.

"In general the market was quiet. (Banks) covered short positions they were left with yesterday, after the Fed decided not to raise interest rates," said Pablo Perrusquia, a peso trader with the Inverlat brokerage.
The benchmark 48-hour and the 24-hour peso closed 0.8 and 0.7 centavo lower, respectively, at 7.5300/7.5350 and 7.5250/7.5300 per dollar.
"Volume, apart from swaps, was lower than in recent sessions. There was no demand from foreigners, they just recycled their funds," he added.
The same-day peso earlier closed 0.8 firmer at 7.5200/7.5240 per dollar
Traders said swap trades entailed selling dollars in the same-day market, then buying them back in the 24-hour and 48-hour markets.
Some analysts said volume was thin due to caution following higher-than-expected inflation figures and local primary rates assigned Tuesday.
They expect the peso to trade between 7.52 and 7.55 for the rest of this week.
